newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chips lift Morocco's bourse slightly.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lift Morocco's bourse slightly.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange closed on Thursday 0.14 percent higher, with the market picking up after more than a month of decline, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 620.06 points from 619.19 points on Wednesday.

"The declining trend of these last weeks made stocks cheaper and consequently more attractive for potential buyers but this slight rise should be taken cautiously, the market can still go down," a broker at BMCI Securities said.
First Moroccan private holding ONA Group rose 22 dirhams to 762 dirhams with 14,380 shares traded.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group, was up 19 dirhams to 680 with more than 10,000 shares changing hands.
In the banking sector, Banque Commerciale du Maroc rose 22 dirhams to 775s and Wafabank gained 21 dirhams to 738.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir fell 10 dirhams to close at 359.95. Steel mill Sonasid also fell, shedding 15 dirhams to 509.
Credit firm Credor went down 20 dirhams to 663 and Maroc Leasing dropped 12 dirhams to 417. Portfolio firm Financiere Diwan gained 10 dirhams to 363.

Total traded volume on the official market was 100.4 million dirhams from 63.2 million. On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 94.1 million dirhams from 48.7 million. Main trade on this market was 21,445 shares in fertilizer firm Fertima FERT.CS, followed by Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie with 20,000 shares exchanged.
